meta.title: Skydance: Two Studios, One Balance Sheet
meta.dek: David Ellison bought Warner Bros. Discovery with $57 billion of new secured debt and $47 billion of equity at $12 a share. Six weeks later the stock is [[price]]. Is the market wrong about the plan, or right about the debt?
meta.price_note: Nov 18, 2026, 10:47 AM ET (StockAnalysis real-time; the Yahoo quote page was stale at the Oct 27 print)
meta.type: Media conglomerate: linear TV networks, streaming subscriptions and film/TV studios
meta.stage: Levered merger integration (mature ex-growth linear funding a streaming build)

verdict.sentence: Two studios, the deepest library in the business and $87 billion of debt: at [[price]] the probability-weighted case pays [[pw_return]] a year against the 13% hurdle, because about $6 billion of synergies has to cover about $6 billion of new interest before shareholders keep anything.
verdict.breaks_if: net leverage is still above 6× at the end of 2027, or Skydance issues equity below $12. Then the Bear is a funding loop and the stock is an option on the lenders' goodwill, not an investment.
verdict.next: ~early Mar 2027 (Q4, FY2027 guide, pro forma financials)
verdict.compounding: n/m (2026 base depressed by new interest; see Valuation)

call: Skydance has fallen 43% below the $12 at which its new owners bought 3.9 billion shares six weeks ago, though the quarter it just reported beat guidance. The market is pricing the balance sheet, not the quarter: about $87 billion of gross debt, roughly $6 billion a year of interest and $20.3 billion maturing within five years. At [[price]] the price implies about a [[implied_bear]] chance of the Bear, where linear declines 9% a year, leverage breaches the 5.5× covenant and equity is raised. I put that at 30%, because the last merger of these same cable networks delivered its synergies and still shrank. The Base, where the savings mostly arrive but linear erosion eats half of it, is worth [[Base.value]]; management's plan in full is the Bull at [[Bull.value]]. Weighted, that is [[pw_ev]] and [[pw_return]] a year, below the 13% hurdle at any plausible Bear probability (break-even [[breakeven_bear]]). The one number that settles it is the 2027 guide in early March: adjusted EBITDA up from about $12.4 billion and free cash flow at or above breakeven after cost to achieve.

tests.claim: That the synergy plan reaches the P&L faster than linear erodes.
tests.test: at the Q4 2026 print (~early March 2027), pro forma FY2026 adjusted EBITDA ≥$12.0B, FY2027 guidance of adjusted EBITDA ≥$13.5B, and FY2027 free cash flow guided at or above breakeven after cost to achieve ([source: Q3 call](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/10/skydance-skyd-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)).
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Base to Bear (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test1.verb]]**, entry [[test1.entry]]; the holder verb becomes Exit if the guide also shows FY2027 FCF below zero.

tests.claim: That linear declines at a manageable rate.
tests.test: pro forma TV Media revenue down no more than 8% year over year in each of Q1 and Q2 2027, excluding political advertising, and no top-tier sports package (NFL on CBS, March Madness, TNT's NHL/MLB) lost or cut at renewal.
tests.if_fail: Base cut to $7.28 on an 8% annual linear decline (PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test2.verb]]**, entry [[test2.entry]].

tests.claim: That the balance sheet de-levers from cash flow, not from shareholders.
tests.test: net leverage on the company's definition at or below 5.5× at year-end 2027 and falling, the $0.05 quarterly dividend kept, and no primary equity issued below $12. Asset sales that retire debt at ≥10× EBITDA (DC, non-core networks) count as a pass.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Bull to Bear (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test3.verb]]** for a non-holder and **Exit** for a holder; the funding loop is then live.

return_math.compounding: n/m on the 2026 base. Owner FCF per share is depressed to ≈$0.14 by the new ≈$6B interest bill, so Base growth of [[Base.cagr]] a year is recovery, not compounding, and the multiple falls from ≈50× to 10×. The honest measure: Base FY2031 owner FCF of [[Base.owner_eps]] a share is ≈12% of today's price, plus the [[yield]] dividend.
return_math.price_implied: At 10%, spot needs FY2031 owner FCF of [[Priced-in.owner_eps]] a share at a 10× exit, about a fifth of the way from the Base to the Bull. Perpetual cross-check: EV ≈$114B on ≈$6.2B of FY2026 unlevered FCF after tax [Estimate] implies g ≈4.6% a year forever, more than a business with a shrinking core has shown.
return_math.epv: ≈$1.40 per share: FY2026 owner FCF of ≈$0.7B capitalized at 10% with no growth. On an enterprise basis (≈$12.4B EBITDA less ≈$4.6B of capex and content cash, after tax, at 10%) EPV is ≈$62B against ≈$80B of net debt, so the no-growth equity is worth nothing. About 80% of the price pays for synergies and growth. The Bear ([[Bear.value]]) sits below EPV because it damages today's earnings power (linear −9% a year).
return_math.base_rate: The Bull needs ≈3.3% nominal (≈1% real) revenue growth from $65B; ≈27% of companies over $50B exceed 5% real, so revenue is not the stretch. The stretch is margin: adjusted EBITDA from 19% to 25% while the highest-margin segment shrinks. Bull Plausible, Base and Bear Probable.
return_math.year_ten: In 2036 TV Media is still shrinking and streaming must carry most of the profit; the Base 10× exit implies no growth (implied g 0%), so the terminal multiple is not doing the work. The equity value is in debt paydown, not growth.
return_math.rr_note: . Mechanically flattered: the Bear is close to zero, so the ratio looks like 2:1 while the Bear costs almost all of the stake.
return_math.note: Discount rate 10% (levered, cyclical media). Hurdle 13%. Built with Claude.

scenarios.note: Exit multiples apply to FY2031 owner free cash flow per share (after SBC). Bull 12× ≈8.5×, Base 10× ≈7.9× and Bear 8× ≈7.7× EV/EBITDA on each case's 2031 net debt [Derived]. Priced-in and Hurdle are solved along Base→Bull at 10×. Built with Claude.

model_build.note: Segment "operating profit" is segment adjusted EBITDA. "Corporate and other" carries corporate costs, capex, content cash above amortization and case-specific interest differences; the common interest line (≈$6.0B in 2026, −3% a year) sits between "operating profit" and net income. "Net income" is therefore free cash flow before SBC; owner earnings deduct SBC after tax. FY2026 is the author's pro forma estimate.
